title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page). K is a CM field of degree 2d with maximal totally real subfield K_r. S_K^0 is the connected Serre-type torus attached to K: a quotient of the Weil restriction T_K = R_{K/Q} G_m. Its character group is, up to finite index, the lattice of functions f on Hom(K, Qbar) with f(σ) + f(cσ) constant, so it has rank d+1. For a CM type Σ with reflex field E, ψ_Σ : S_K^0 → T_E is the reflex-norm (type) homomorphism. The previous page proved ψ_Σ ∘ i_K = i_{E/Q} on G_m.

Faithfulness with d+1 CM types (end of previous page and top of this page). Let Σ = {σ_1,…,σ_d} and let Σ_i be Σ with σ_i replaced by its conjugate cσ_i. Suppose x is killed by ψ_Σ and by every ψ_{Σ_i}. Comparing the two types gives σ_i(x) = cσ_i(x) for all i, so x lies in K_r. Then the weight condition forces N_{K_r/Q}(x) = 1, so x lies in the compact part and dies in S_K^0. The NB records that K_r = ∩_i Ker(σ_i, σ̄_i) is stable under base change Q → Λ, so the argument works scheme-theoretically over any coefficient algebra. Hence Ker ψ_Σ ∩ ∩_{i=1}^{d} Ker ψ_{Σ_i} = 1 in S_K^0. In character language: Σ together with the differences Σ − Σ_i = σ_i − cσ_i span the rank-(d+1) character lattice, so only d+1 well-chosen reflex norms are needed rather than all CM types.

Question. Restrict to the ψ_Σ whose reflex field E is (imaginary) quadratic. Is their common kernel finite? These ψ_Σ are exactly the CM types induced from imaginary quadratic subfields E ⊂ K, and then ψ_Σ = N_{K/E}, i.e. the CM-elliptic-curve-type characters. So the answer depends on how many quadratic subfields K has. Let L be the subfield generated by the quadratic subfields of K. If L ≠ K, i.e. Gal is not (Z/2)^N, then Ker(N_{K/L} : S_K^0 → S_L^0) is a torus of dimension d − d_L > 0 lying in the kernel of all these ψ. So the answer is no unless K is multiquadratic.

The marginal '(?Weil)' seems to point towards Weil-type objects as the needed supplement. The motivic reading is: CM motives of K are (up to isogeny) generated by Hecke characters of imaginary quadratic fields, i.e. by CM elliptic curves, only when K is generated by quadratic fields.
errors: Not an error but an omission: the converse is not stated on the page. When Gal(K/Q) = (Z/2)^N, the odd characters χ of G correspond bijectively to the imaginary quadratic subfields. The norms N_{K/E} pull back exactly trivial + χ, so they jointly have finite kernel on S_K^0 (dimension 2^{N-1}+1). The criterion is therefore 'iff', for Galois K at least.
The transcription's 'tore de dim 0' should be 'dim > 0' for the argument to make sense.
The 'donc x = V'_{K_r}' step on the previous page means x lies in the compact (norm-one) part, which is trivial in S_K^0. This is fine but tersely stated.

ideas.what: Kernel of the reflex-norm homomorphisms for the d+1 CM types Σ, Σ_1,…,Σ_d is trivial in the connected Serre torus S_K^0, functorially in the coefficient ring
ideas.modern_name: Serre group S^K as image of T_K under reflex norms (Serre 1968; Milne–Shih 1982); spanning of the CM-type lattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968); Langlands, Milne–Shih for the Taniyama group/Serre group formalism

ideas.what: Question whether reflex norms to imaginary quadratic fields (CM elliptic curve characters) detect S_K^0; answer negative unless K is generated by its quadratic subfields, via the positive-dimensional kernel of N_{K/L}
ideas.modern_name: CM motives/Hecke characters generated by CM elliptic curves only for multiquadratic CM fields; need for Weil-type classes (André's reduction of CM Hodge classes to Weil classes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related results by Shioda, Schappacher (Periods of Hecke characters, 1988), Deligne (1982), André (1992)

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies that the 'quadratic' reflex norms fail to be faithful exactly when K is not multiquadratic. The marginal '(? Weil)' suggests he saw the need for a supplementary class of objects. This anticipates the later fact (Deligne, André 1992) that Hodge classes on CM abelian varieties are generated by Weil classes attached to imaginary quadratic fields, rather than by CM elliptic curves. The thread is not developed on the page.
missed.quote: il faut voir s'il y a "nb" des (?Weil) sous-corps quadratiques de K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically shows Grothendieck in the 1960s probing which 'elementary' CM motives generate the motivic Galois group of CM motives. This is the same question later resolved via Weil classes. Of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Early (pre-Serre-1968, if the dating holds) handling of the Serre torus via reflex norms and a clean faithfulness criterion. All of the mathematics is elementary and known or folklore; interest is mainly historical.
transcription_corrections: 'tore de dim 0' should likely read 'tore de dim > 0'.

Garbled passage likely reads: 'Si K n'est pas engendré par ses sous-corps quadratiques, i.e. si son groupe de Galois n'est pas (Z/2Z)^N, alors le noyau de N_{K/L} : S_K^0 → S_L^0 est un tore de dim > 0 qui est dans le noyau de tous les ψ_Σ envisagés' (L = subfield generated by quadratic subfields).
Line 'Y a-t-il un nb fini...' plausibly 'y a-t-il un noyau fini' (is the common kernel finite).
'L'hom ψ_K correspondant à N_{K/E}' should be 'l'hom ψ_Σ correspondant est N_{K/E}' (for Σ induced from a quadratic E ⊂ K).
